newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends higher, cash gains supportive.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends higher, cash gains supportive.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed higher with buying late in the session sparked by the activation of chart-based buy orders, traders said.
Early gains were the result of continued buying after Thursday's sharply higher to limit gains and on news early Friday that cash lumber prices were recovering from an early-week slump.
Analysts and traders said lumber dealers appear to be rebuilding inventories which has produced a firm tone in wholesale lumber prices.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $354 per thousand board feet Friday, up $4 from midweek, but down $4 from a week ago.
CME lumber closed up $6.70 to $0.10 per tbf, with July up the most a $369.10 and September up $0.30 at $354.50.
